page.title: Factions
page.t:
Cut off from the Empire's leadership, and with much of the local religious structure lost in a freak navigational accident, the Paranid inhabitants of Wretched Skies spent much of the Shutdown building an unusual bond of blood with their Split neighbors through constant violent clashes. 

Strangely, the influence of the Split had something of a stabilizing effect on these leaderless Paranid; rather than descending into madness or despondence, the Paranid of Wretched Skies rallied around a new doctrine that combined scattered elements of the traditional Paranid mythos with the brutal tenets of Split culture. Once the Gates reopened, this earned them the respect of the Split Patriarch, but also the enmity of both the Godrealm and the Holy Order, a position which is held mutually by the Faithful. Unlike the Holy Order, they are much less concerned about the heresies of the "lesser races" and maintain generally nonhostile, if somewhat chilly, relationships with most other Commonwealth powers. 

The fanatical beliefs of Xaar's Faithful are simple, straightforward, and impossibly heretical to the larger Paranid factions. According to the Faithful, the continued absence of Paranid Prime from the known Gate Network is no mere accident. They hold that the Priest-Emperor has shrouded the system from sight, biding his time in the darkness between the stars as a trial laid upon all Paranid, and that he someday will return to lead the Paranid people once more: embracing those who remained devoted, rewarding those who took up arms in his name, and cleansing all apostates with holy fire. As was decreed fitting of their position as subservient to the Priest-Emperor, no Paranid of Xaar's Faithful may hold a title above Deacon, and thus Xaarist affairs are generally directed by the "Deacon Triumvirate" - a triplet of councils representing the dogmatic pillars of Belief in Xaar, Force of Arms, and Mundanity of Life.

OTAS (Optimised Technology, Armaments and Shielding Corporation)

The Optimised Technology, Armaments and Shielding Corporation, commonly known as OTAS, is a omnicorporation specialized in the design and manufacture of advanced spaceships heaquartered in Legend's Home. In the pre-Shutdown era, OTAS technologies and ships were highly advanced, often leading the cutting edge of Commonwealth scientific advancement, granting the corporation a prominent position on the political starscape of the old Commonweath of Planets.

Just prior to the Great Collapse, OTAS launched an attack on Akeela's Beacon in an escalatory response to the passing of certain industry regulations by the Argon Federation. Seen as an act of terrorism by the Argon, the resulting Argon military response was cut short by Gate Shutdown. While the exact history of the period is lost to the chaos of the Great Dark, it is clear that the Argon response failed to bring OTAS to heel and the corporation now holds full administrative and military control of the formerly Argon sectors in their local region. 

Having evolved beyond a simple technologies corporation, the massive OTAS commercial enterprise now operates as a fully independent star nation. Featuring locally appointed representatives from each controlled sector sitting on the board of directors and a functional state apparatus that earns generally favourable public sentiment, any scars of the hostile takeover have seemingly faded from memory.

While very much still human, and thus biologically indistinguishable from Argon citizens, the citizens of the OTAS corporation-state have developed culturally into a distinct pseudo-corporate society during their isolation. Following the reconnection, OTAS citizens have come to be seen by much of the Commonwealth as a mixture of both the Argon and Terrans in ambition, technology, and temperament. Only time will tell if they continue to carve their own path or are ultimately brought back into the fold.

page.title: Ships
page.t: In the midst of the Terran War, the Argon Federation floundered somewhat in their ship design output. Perhaps their worst effort was the Quasar fighter, which, named after a powerful cosmic force, failed to fully live up to expectations.

Redesigned using the same combat-ready cockpit used by the new-look Nova, the Eclipse replaces the rotatable engines with a support structure that allows it to carry more weapons - effectively sacrificing the manoeuvrability of the dog-fighter for enough fire-power to be devastating against both small- and medium-sized ships.\n\nThis sacrifice does make the ship vulnerable to more specialised dog-fighters and interceptors, but nonetheless the Federal navy has found the new Eclipse to be a worthy addition to their fleets, with Argon ship designers once again leading the race to design ships effective for both personal and military use.

Designed, built, and put into service with staggering and uncharacteristic alacrity by the Argon Federation Navy, the Buster is the result of Argon efforts to swiftly close the capabilities gap posed by the OTAS Notus and Split Wolf bombers. 

Unlike many of its peers, the Buster as a combat machine is wholly unremarkable, backing up it's single bomber-class hardpoint with a pair of conventional light weapons mounts and featuring a singular shield projector, the ship trades individual power for expedience in service and an exceptionally low production cost.

Thanks to the Argon Navy's numerous external threats and competing priorities, it has thus far maintained that "the ship you have now is better than a ship you might have next year" and the Buster has remained in service with no replacement in sight despite its various shortcomings, much to the annoyance of its pilots. Many common jokes within Argon Buster squadrons pointedly highlight the attractiveness of the ship's low cost of production and operation to the Argon civilian government, laced with macabre punchlines wondering how many Busters must be destroyed before it becomes economically advantageous to develop an improved ship. However, this same affordability has resulted in the Buster finding a surprisingly successful market among small independent mercenary outfits or private security firms, where the ship represents a very cheap opportunity to augment marketable capabilities.

As the first highly-anticipated combat-line product launched by the post-shutdown reconsolidated Jonferson Space Dynamics Division, the Mk3 Centaur is a dramatic return to the ship's roots as a fast, aggressive corvette-class striker. Designed in a bid to produce a ship capable of matching or exceeding the capabilities of the venerable Terran Katana, the ship boasts a formidable array of forward weaponry, good all-around turret coverage and fighter-like agility, though this comes at the cost of a light-duty hull structure and somewhat mediocre overall protection.\n\nWith the newly-reformed company holding a tenuous financial position, it was a deliberate decision by Jonferco designers to recall the classic Argon design in a bid for a knockout market entrance. Though the Centaur fell somewhat short of the impossibly lofty expectations set upon it by Jonferco executive leadership, the ship proved a commercial and military success, being well liked by its users and earning a particular popularity with the semi-independent Special Action Task Forces of the Argon and Antigone navies.

The Baku is a heavily militarized adaptation of the Drill miner, initially conceived as a Blockade Runner. Upgraded with enhanced shielding, improved weapon systems, and increased speed, the Baku trades its mining capabilities for versatility in combat and cargo operations. Its cargo hold has been reconfigured to carry standard container wares, while a significant expansion of crew accommodations allows it to host an unusually large complement for its class. These features make the Baku a favorite among pirate crews, who value its well-rounded combination of speed, firepower, and cargo capacity - along with its ability to deploy multiple boarding teams during daring raids.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: CmdrTurianes [SVE]\033X\

The Argon Orthrus is in many ways the archetypical example of the class, with average shielding and mobility backed up by a pair of M-class turrets for self defense, supporting a wing of four fighters.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The latest redesign of the Mercury-class transporter was almost purely aesthetic, with only small changes made to allow the user more modularity and modification options. Other than the aesthetic changes made to keep the model in line with latest style trends, the Mercury remains the same reliable M-sized transporter that has seen popular use across Argon space for so many years.

Known for its versatility and dependable design, the Mercury Passenger Transport - sometimes nostalgically called the "Express" - is the Commonwealth's most balanced passenger vessel. Built on the sturdy, modular Mercury chassis, this transport offers an ideal mix of speed and capacity, making it a popular choice for everyday intersector travel. While its interiors are comfortable and thoughtfully designed, they steer clear of excessive luxury, providing an efficient, no-nonsense environment for passengers. Reliable and well-rounded, the Mercury Passenger Transport remains a trusted workhorse for Argon and Commonwealth alike, getting travelers to their destinations smoothly and on time.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

Often referred to as the 'Centaur II' by its captains due to a close resemblance and planned replacement for that icoic ship, the Cyclops was developed as a response to increasing Xenon fighter swarm activity. Sporting excellent speed for its size and bristling with tightly grouped anti-fighter turret systems it is an effective anti-fighter escort for larger capital ships. It's speed also makes the Cyclops perfect for exploration and reconnaissance activities and it has therefore become the go-to vessel for Argon secret service operations.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Axeface [Argon Cyclops - Deluxe Edition]\033X\

The original design of the Behemoth-class destroyer was put into development mid-way through the Kha'ak conflict, during which the Titan-class was beginning to show its age and inefficiencies. At first too expensive for a crippled Argon economy, then too complex to produce quickly during the Terran Conflict, the first Behemoth did not ship out until long after that war had ended, and the Jump Gates had begun to catastrophically fail. It was only when Argon Prime and Black Hole Sun came back into contact that the Behemoth could be rolled out more frequently - and then, after being delayed by over 50 years and never properly tested - combat deployments of the vessel revealed a critical flaw in power delivery systems. In a bid to salvage the, already mass produced, design - main weapons and High-Energy mounts have been stripped in order to turn the ship into a viable escort frigate.

The original design of the Behemoth-class destroyer was put into development mid-way through the Kha'ak conflict, during which the Titan-class was beginning to show its age and inefficiencies. At first too expensive for a crippled Argon economy, then too complex to produce quickly during the Terran Conflict, the first Behemoth did not ship out until long after that war had ended, and the Jump Gates had begun to catastrophically fail. It was only when Argon Prime and Black Hole Sun came back into contact that the Behemoth could be rolled out more frequently - and then, after being delayed by over 50 years and never properly tested - combat deployments of the vessel revealed a critical flaw in power delivery systems. In a bid to salvage the, already mass produced, design - large turret mounts have been stripped in order to turn the ship into a viable assault frigate.

While relatively lightly armed for a destroyer, the modern Behemoth, also known as "Enhanced Behemoth" does not suffer from power delivery issues that plagued its predecessor. As a result all turret mounts sport sufficient tracking systems and capacitors to allow mounting either Point-Defense or High-Energy weapons in any slot, leading to the vessel being recognized as the most configurable destroyer in the Commonwealth.

The Argon Charybdis, based on the venerable pre-Shutdown M7 Cerberus-class chassis, is a modernized adaptation designed to fulfill the Argon Federation’s long-range offensive needs. While retaining the iconic structure and agility of the Cerberus frigate, this new variant sacrifices conventional firepower for an extensive array of advanced missile launchers. Equipped to maintain a continuous stream of individually tracking missiles, it effectively dominates targets at long distances, striking from afar while remaining highly mobile.

Although its defensive weapon systems are modest, with only four medium turrets and a single shield, the Charybdis is fitted with an expanded drone bay and two dedicated launch tubes, allowing it to rapidly deploy a fleet of defensive drones. This adaptation ensures that, despite its light direct defenses, the frigate remains well-protected against threats that breach its missile range. Prioritizing speed, firepower at range, and tactical drone support, this missile frigate represents Argon commitment to supplementing relatively light warships with consumables and expendable, unmanned craft.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: ArgonMatt & Rothank\033X\

Scylla represents the latest Argon attempt to merge carrier functionality with frontline support, purpose-built to escort and match pace with Behemoth-class destroyers. Following years of limited carrier options that lacked effective escort capabilities, the Scylla was envisioned as a hybrid platform - one capable of deploying support craft while holding its own against fighter swarms.

Armed with large-caliber point-defense turrets and outfitted with respectable shielding, the Scylla straddles the line between light carrier and escort frigate. Yet, in seeking to fulfill both roles, it falls short of excelling in either. Its fighter capacity is the lowest in class - reminiscent of the Griffon of the pre-Shutdown era - and its speed insufficient to accompany faster vessels. However, expanded drone bays provide some compensation, enabling flexible engagement profiles and robust automated defense.

The ship’s development was anything but smooth. Conflicting design philosophies led to an extended and costly prototyping phase. According to internal sources, the final production blueprint was misplaced for nearly fourteen months - a bureaucratic mishap that only deepened the vessel’s reputation for troubled beginnings.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Entissus & Rothank\033X\

Though the Sonra-class freighter was initially designed by Terracorp after the Terran Conflict, the status of development was lost with contact to Home of Light. Quite by chance, project designers were trapped in Black Hole Sun during the Jump Gate shutdown, and were able to get the blueprints of the finished ship to the Jonferco corporation when contact with Belt of Aguilar was re-established.

Designed and produced by the Antigone Republic after the Jump Gates began to realign, the Veles-class freighter is more compact and self-sufficient than any freighter-class ship before it; the reason why it became part of the on-going technology exchange between the Republic and their Argon Federation allies.\n\nBuilt using a highly modular design, many ship designers have taken the base Veles model and reorganised it, as well as making their own changes to the internal systems, to sell an ever-growing number of variations on the ship. However, the Veles remains a popular choice among traders and station builders.

Only very recently developed, the Argon Leviathan is the current apex of Argon military technology, found patrolling core Argon sectors which require the most impenetrable defense. For combat ships of such a large caliber, the Leviathan packs well rounded characteristics. It boasts an impressive array of weaponry; the surface of the Leviathan is bristling with an extensive array of turrets rendering small fighter incursions against the Leviathan largely inconsequential, and simultaneously augments the Leviathan's anti capital capability. The Leviathan is essentially an expansive mobile fortress, and any force brave enough to assault this beast should conduct attacks with extreme caution.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: ArgonMatt [Argon Leviathan - XL Battleship]\033X\

The final ship shared with the Argon Federation by the Antigone Republic as part of their ongoing technology exchange, the new-look Colossus-class carrier was initially designed as such so that it didn't use much-needed resources that were sorely lacking in Antigone Memorial during the Jump Gate shutdown.\n\nWith an array of medium and small docks and launch tubes, the Antigone Colossus is a significant improvement on older Colossus models, able to deploy ships to the battlefield at a much higher rate and collect and store them far more efficiently, at the cost of some of its previous firepower.

A compact, sphere-shaped defense drone favored by Teladi traders as a reliable distraction during high-risk retreats. Small, highly agile, and unusually well-shielded for its class, the Sparrow is designed to draw enemy fire away from its mothership rather than engage in prolonged combat. While its offensive systems are minimal, swarms of Sparrows can confuse targeting systems and create the illusion of greater resistance than actually present, allowing their more valuable operators to escape unharmed.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The cigar boat of the X universe, the Kestrel is obscenely fast, not terribly maneuverable, and well-suited for smuggling contraband. As mainstream military technology turned toward improved heavy fighters and lighter, more mobile capital ships, Teladi shipwrights saw a profit opportunity for a ship fast enough to stay clear of police patrols and, when necessary, break through military blockades.

The Kea combines respectable speed, shielding and armament to create a well-rounded starship capable of tackling any challenge. In classic fashion Teladi shipwrights managed to squeeze an oversized cargo bay into this vessels small frame, compensating for this extra weight with far more engines than is usually necessary for a ship of this size. The sluggish agility resulting from all this extra equipment has lead many crews to refer to this new addition to the Teladi lineup as (loosely translated) "The Brick".\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Axeface [Teladi Kea]\033X\

The Teladi Jacana boasts above-average shielding, hull integrity and cargo capacity, though it possesses the typically below-average mobility and poor armament found on civilian Teladi designs.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Teladi Vulture medium freighter, while generally unassuming, remains a popular choice for independent traders in particular. It has excellent cargo capacity, more than making up for its lack of speed, on an analysis of trade route profitability.

The Teladi Vulture medium freighter, while generally unassuming, remains a popular choice for independent traders in particular. It has excellent cargo capacity, more than making up for its lack of speed, on an analysis of trade route profitability.

The Teladi Vulture Passenger Transport may not be the fastest vessel in the stars, but what it lacks in speed, it more than makes up for in sheer capacity. Boasting the highest passenger count among all currently produced transports, the Vulture is the go-to choice for those looking to move large numbers in one journey. Retrofitted with amenities comparable to the Argon Mercury passenger variant, the Vulture offers comfortable seating, climate control, and spacious lounges, providing a pleasant travel experience for its passengers. Despite its unhurried pace, the Vulture’s reliability and high capacity make it an invaluable asset for mass transit across vast distances.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

One of the more unusual ships produced by the Teladi Company, the Cassowary frigate is something of an engineering and marketing oddity. Abruptly released to the market with little fanfare shortly after the launch of the Heron E, critical observers have noted the ship's resemblance to a truncated forward dome section of the larger Heron freighter. The Teladi Company has vehemently denied allegations that the Cassowary is simply a repurposed Heron hull section that suffered structural failure during construction, with one Teladi Company spokesperson being quoted as saying that "The front section did not 'fall off' of anything! If anything, the Cassowary IS the front!". The Teladi Company has since distanced itself from the quoted official and has not acknowledged any requests for clarification.

Unusual appearance notwithstanding, the Cassowary is an uncharacteristically well-armed offering in the Teladi catalogue. Boasting no less than three large turret hardpoints and protected by two large shield projectors, the ship is a superlative standout in the frigate class, though it is notably lacking in mdedium-sized point-defense armament compared to its peers and suffers from a significant aft blindspot due to the unique hull layout.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Teladi-built Ostrich superfreighter is a marvel of interstellar engineering, designed for optimal versatility and maximum cost-efficiency. Equipped with expansive cargo holds and adaptive cargo handling systems, these flagship freighters can transport virtually any type of ware, be it traditionally processed and packed container goods or raw bulk resources, making the Ostrich an attractive choice for those particularly economical captains who desire to truly squeeze every possible credit from their trade runs. But, contrary to the vigorous assertions of some Teladi tycoons, the value of a freighter is found in more than the simple depths of their cargo spaces - after all, no matter how large the load, it must be moved to its destination in order to realise a profit. In this field the Ostrich excels, boasting an atypically excellent thrust-to-mass ratio that distinguishes the ship from both its peers and most other Teladi products and cementing its status as an exciting and widely sought-after offering from the Teladi Company Shipbuilding Section.

One of the Ostrich's most striking visual characteristics is the highly unusual and somewhat anachronistic spin gravity system employed for its cargo storage sections. Consisting of two contrarotating hull sections with the primary cargo holds held in outboard pods, the system maintains a comfortable (for the Teladi) 0.9G of perceived gravity to provide stable conditions for the ship's working crew and any sensitive cargo aboard. Touted as a cost-saving measure compared to traditional artificial gravity systems, the Ostrich's spin mechanism must nevertheless be carefully maintained and calibrated. These risks were made starkly apparent by an incident just prior to the prototype's maiden voyage, when Inspecting Engineer Nisturios Epistimios Egomatistis IV discovered a critical software error in the ship's spin controller module which would have resulted in the outer pods (including the converted banquet spaces full of functionaries within) experiencing a crushing 12G of force. Thanks to this narrowly avoided disaster, all production model Ostrich freighters possess a redesigned spin controller which uses a purely mechanical system to enforce a constant 0.9G spin rate, thus freeing the Teladi Company from any liability concerns involving a programmable module.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank & Entissus\033X\

As much a product of cultural dogma as one of military necessity, the Paranid Cupid defence drone was initially designed by the Holy Order to both provide their forces with a combat advantage and to free their captains from the perceived shame of relying on the heretical Standard drone. The Holy Order enjoyed a brief period of drone superiority before the design was acquired by the Godrealm, which swiftly adopted the system and began to field their own copy. 

Armed with dual Paranid PALCs, the Cupid gives Paranid forces a unique form of offensive support.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Entissus & Rothank\033X\
A fast, small interceptor, with respectable hardpoints, the Paranid Perseus has a reasonable following among fighter pilots and explorers alike.
The Paranid Theseus is a solid, all-round performer with deadly firepower, built upon a solid chassis.
The Ares meets the much demanded need for a Paranid Heavy Fighter. Loaded with weapon hard points and shield generators, the Ares can both take and deliver a beating - at the cost of mobility.

Recognizing the strategic advantage of long-range firepower, the Paranid command selected the swift and agile Artemis as the foundation for their new heavy-hitting unit. Its sibling, the Apollo, trades some of the Artemis’s famed agility for a substantial upgrade: nearly double the internal storage capacity, allowing it to carry a formidable payload of Prism cruise missiles. This transformation turns the Apollo into a potent, long-range bombardment vessel, capable of delivering relentless firepower from afar.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Lint5 [Artemis], modified by: Rothank\033X\

The Paranid Helianthus is a fairly minimal modification of the Demeter, simply extending the chassis and replacing many of the outer-hull storage units with an array of micro-tractor emitters. Though lightly armed, like its transporter ancestor the Helianthus boasts improved shielding and excellent mobility.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\
The Demeter is a medium-sized Paranid-designed journeyman freighter with reasonable performance.
The Demeter is a medium-sized Paranid-designed journeyman freighter with reasonable performance.

The Demeter Passenger Transport redefines luxury travel for discerning passengers seeking both speed and comfort. Though it offers a more limited capacity due to its commitment to first-class standards, this Paranid-designed vessel spares no expense in providing high-end amenities. Elegant interiors, plush seating, and exclusive lounges ensure a refined experience for every traveler. As the second fastest M-sized passenger transport in the universe, the Demeter combines speed with sophistication, making it the premier choice for those who value both efficiency and extravagance on their journeys.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Paranid Odysseus is a highly regarded destroyer with an often consequential presence in large scale engagements. Modern variants prioritise hardpoints, however, they suffers from reduced mobility as a consequence.

Engineered to lead Paranid military strikes, the Artemis frigate is a powerful yet streamlined vessel, built for efficiency and impact. Armed with two imposing forward-facing large weapon mounts, it packs a punch that makes it a formidable spearhead in any assault. Its straightforward construction keeps production costs surprisingly low for a Paranid design, but there's a trade-off: the Artemis has a significant vulnerability in point defense, leaving it exposed to smaller, more agile threats. This balance of power and cost makes the Artemis a bold choice for commanders willing to push the offensive.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Lint5, modified by: Rothank\033X\

A highly conventional application of Split combat philosophy, the Split-designed Skink defence drone is extremely fast and mounts a deadly Mass Driver as the main weapon system, giving it an unexpected edge in combat when facing larger targets.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Entissus & Rothank\033X\

The Split Wolf bomber is one of the largest and deadliest S-class combat ships, surpassing even the powerful Chimera. Developed with the assistance of OTAS engineers under a diplomatic effort to cooperate against their enemy, the Argon Federation, the Wolf makes use of technologies first pioneered for the OTAS Notus bomber, adapted for the generally lower Commonwealth technology base. Though relatively slow and a large target, the Wolf has a powerful arsenal of weapons fitted to a heavily reinforced hull, and in numbers presents a formidable threat to capital-class targets of any size. 

With the Wolf demonstrating an integration of OTAS and Commonwealth engineering, the technology soon spread through the Gate Network, with other powers fielding their own bomber-type vessels.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Brummbear, modified by: Rothank\033X\

The Crocodile is a makeshift combat ship produced by Free Families following their defeat against the Patriarchy. Since the Crocodile is built on the hull of the Alligator, it primarily relies on speed rather than defences to survive. While the Iguana features a slightly increased hull integrity compared to its sistership, it can not stand up against any comparable gunship in a direct fight. Most of the original storage components of the ship have been converted to house servers meant to support computational load required by Point-Defense weaponry and weight savings allowed to drastically increase max speed.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: CmdrTurianes [SVE]\033X\

The Split-built Iguana is one of the smallest ships in the class, though it still manages to land a wing of four heavy fighters and features the aggressive speed common to Split designs.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\
Nowhere in the owner's manual is the Boa explicitly described as a smuggling vessel. Law-abiding pilots insist that the ship's surprising speed is used to outrun pirates.

Nowhere in the owner's manual is the Boa explicitly described as a smuggling vessel. Law-abiding pilots insist that the ship's surprising speed is used to outrun pirates. \n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

A straightforward passenger conversion of the cargo-hauling Boa, this transport offers lighting fast option for moving passengers across Commonwealth space. Designed to prioritize speed over comfort, the Boa’s passenger variant sacrifices amenities, featuring cramped quarters and limited facilities that provide only the essentials. With a compact interior originally intended for cargo, passengers should expect minimal comforts and close quarters. However, its swift travel capabilities and dependable design make the Boa ideal for those who need reliable transit—even if luxury takes a backseat.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

A simple conversion of the popular mining ship - Caiman has been specifically designed to avoid raising suspicion from Zyarth police. Disabling all drone-control systems freed up enough processing power to allow upgrading all turret mounts to meet requirements of Point-Defense weaponry, turning this ship into a fully capable escort frigate.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: CmdrTurianes [SVE]\033X\

Faced with the ever-increasingly irritating task of policing Free Families colonial space against progressively more creative threats cooked up by Fallen Families warbands, Zyarth forces found themselves in need of a more powerful rapid response and escort vessel than the ubiquitous Cobras and Dragons that ordinarily formed the backbone of colonial police forces. Initial plans to employ the Rattlesnake in this role were met with great enthusiasm from Split captains, but were denied due to the perceived expense of "wasting" a frontline combat vessel on police duty. Unexpectedly, it was Family Kritt which approached the Patriarch with a new design to fulfill the role - the Adder frigate. 

Mounting a large and conspicuous turret battery primarily consisting of anti-fighter weaponry, the Adder is an impressively optimized design - visually impressive, fast, well-armed, and most importantly, much cheaper to manufacture than the Rattlesnake. Among its peers, the Adder boasts a massive array of medium turrets matched with a characteristically strong Split-built hull and powerful engines, providing Zyarth colonial police with a robust fleet leader when engaging ships such as the Free Families Cheetah. The ship has also become a common sight in Split frontline formations, where its high speed and powerful screening armament provides an excellent complement to the immense raw firepower of the Rattlesnake, allowing Split forces to continue to operate even with heavy enemy fighter presence.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

By stripping away much of the Buffalo's original cargo space and overhauling its subsystems for military applications, the Taipan transforms a utilitarian hauler into a formidable warship.

Equipped with advanced High-Energy and Point-Defense weaponry, the Taipan boasts enough firepower to fulfill the role of a midline destroyer, excelling in offensive engagements and fleet operations. However, its retrofit nature comes with compromises - lacking the survivability and structural integrity of purpose-built destroyers, it relies on its mobility and the sheer ferocity of its weapon systems to dominate opponents before they can exploit its vulnerabilities.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: CmdrTurianes [SVE]\033X\

The Ouroboros-class Battleship, secretly developed by the Court of Curbs, is a revolutionary departure from traditional Split warship design. Unlike the fast and aggressive vessels typically associated with the Split, the Ouroboros prioritizes survivability and calculated engagement. Equipped with advanced shielding systems for exceptional durability, it is built to withstand sustained enemy attacks while delivering devastating indirect firepower through its array of guided missile launchers.

Designed to outlast and outmaneuver foes tactically rather than physically, the Ouroboros is a unique asset in the Split fleet - a battleship that challenges expectations while redefining the potential of Split engineering and strategy.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: BZDBQG, modified by: Rothank\033X\
\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Brummbear, modified by: Rothank & Entissus\033X\

Designed in a bid to reduce casualty risk to fighter pilots, the Mobula defense drone is a very agile drone armed with a single low-powered Ion Beam. 

According to Boron fleet doctrine, correct usage of the Mobula drone in a coordinated fleet action sees it deployed in large numbers alongside manned fighters, using its physical presence to distract enemy fire and the engine-disrupting properties of the Ion weaponry to pull apart enemy formations, thus allowing crewed fighters to deliver decisive tactical strikes in relative safety.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Alessandro Cornacchia [CG Artist], "Boronized" by Rothank\033X\

Commissioned by the Atreus Shipbuilding Currents corporation, the Boron Angel is an elegant fusion of luxury, speed, and defense - a vessel fit for Boron royalty and dignitaries on high-stakes journeys. This light, nimble personal transport serves as both a yacht and an armed guardian, combining swift maneuverability with respectable firepower. Though small, it is equipped with magnetic locks capable of docking a single S-class ship, allowing for even more versatility.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

Further building on the success of the Dolphin transporter, the Pleco is a result of a joint effort between Atreus Shipbuilding Currents and Stellar Shores Shipping to develop a mid-size TM-type vessel. Though using the same grav-harness docking technology as most TMs, the unique hull form and docking arrangement of the Pleco allows it to carry no less than six parasite fighters, giving it a distinct edge in offensive capabilities compared to its peers, despite its poor speed. Coupled with the characteristically sturdy Boron shielding, the Pleco makes for a far more dangerous opponent than its spindly appearance and unassuming name might suggest.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Dolphin transporter project largely built upon lessons learnt in prior developments, but also saw new innovations and subsystems designed by students and professors of the Royal Academy of Space Engineering. This cooperation proved to be fruitful for both Atreus Shipbuilding Currents, and for the students, who would gain professional experience and grow to become valuable engineers in the field, either by working directly for the company or founding their own. The Dolphin transporter was released in early 784 (NT).

When the spaciousness of the Dolphin proved inadequate, the Porpoise stepped in to meet the Boron’s demand for a more accommodating passenger vessel. Stripped of its original mining equipment, the Porpoise has been completely refitted to transport passengers in comfort and style. Inside, its compartments have been transformed into large, water-filled “aquarium” rooms, creating a familiar environment for Boron inhabitants. This design allows for smooth and comfortable travel, tailored to the unique needs of its aquatic passengers. With ample interior space and luxurious aquatic amenities, the Porpoise passenger transport offers a seamless journey for Boron travelers across the stars.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The modern incarnation of Terran Keris defence drone is a powerful and advanced semiautomonous weapons system. Though somewhat slower than its Commonwealth counterparts, the Keris presents a reduced target profile and possesses superior armament in the form of a standard Terran Electro-Magnetic Plasma Cannon.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank, based on Cadius' X3 Keris [X3 X-Tra Ship/Station Pack]\033X\

The Terran Falchion bomber is perhaps the most heavily specialized ship in the class. While broadly identical in strategic function as the Notus and other Commonwealth counterparts, the Falchion does not use any version of the Notus' technology, and was developed and built completely from scratch by Terran engineers. 

Unlike other bombers, the Falchion carries no secondary armament to accompany the ordnance hardpoints, and is largely reliant on fighter escorts to clear the battlespace. In exchange, the ship presents a very small target profile and possesses robust shielding, maximizing its survivability against its capital sized targets. 

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Pioneer-built Bulwark is a highly specialized ship for a very specific purpose. Designed to provide small-scale logistics and repair support for stranded civilian vessels and damaged satellite networks, the Bulwark is fitted with a scaled-up version of the standard space suit repair beam and features a unique storage bay to carry a number of disassembled and flat-packed repair drones, though the ship cannot deploy them for usage by itself. In concert with an onboard engineering module capable of assembling or disassembling repair drones in-situ for transfer to a larger ship, the ship's small size belies its remarkable drone carrying capacity, allowing a single Bulwark to effectively get stranded or damaged ships back under way.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Entissus & Rothank\033X\

Reimagined as a hybrid transport that blends personnel mobility with tactical versatility, the Scabbard now serves as both the successor to the Toukon and a redefined version of the original personnel carrier. Built on a reinforced military chassis, this Terran vessel combines the robust durability of the Toukon’s small carrier design with the efficient personnel transfer capabilities of the Scabbard. Unlike its Commonwealth counterparts, this transport sacrifices none of its military-grade capabilities, making it particularly popular among Protectorate black ops forces who value its reliability in high-stakes operations. The Scabbard’s design reflects United Space Command’s commitment to security, efficiency, and adaptability.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

It also adds an extra turret to make it a less attractive target for pirate raids, and to ensure that no wares critical to the Terran war effort are lost in transit.

A ship with a legacy dating to the early years of the Pioneer Initiative, the Pata was born from the Pioneers' need to carefully shepherd all available resources. Derived from the core of the Bolo miner, the Pata is fitted with a larger engine array and a trio of tractor beam projector turrets that allowed the early Pioneers to first clear large debris fields to make navigation safer, and later to recover useful debris and wreckage for salvage and reprocessing. 

Though the faction is no longer as desperately strapped for resources, the conservationist spirit has persisted in the form of more organized salvage operations utilizing purpose-built Patas which constitute a small but culturally important segment of the economy, and the ship's highly distinctive silhouette can be spotted throughout Pioneer space and the bordering regions.

A superlight Terran frigate design that can trace its origins to the end of the Terran Conflict. Although lackluster when facing L-sized ships, it excels at providing anti-strikecraft coverage thanks to unparalleled mobility in its size class and an array of downsized frontal weapons.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Lint5 [Terran Frigates]\033X\

The Yokohama is a slow and heavy frigate equipped with large array of medium turrets, serving as an anti-figther escort within terran battlegroups.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: CmdrTurianes [SVE; original name: Scimtar]\033X\

A refit of Akita. Although visually identical to the Akita-class, the refit is considerably heavier, being designed to devastate enemy stations and ships at extreme ranges - at least while its limited ammunition stores ammunition last. \n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Lint5 [Terran Frigates]\033X\

The Chiba is the Terran refinement of the Pioneers' original converted design. In a rare display of technological acknowledgement, the Terran Protectorate purchased access to the Chiba's design specifications and soon placed an improved version into service. While the design heritage of the Hokkaido hull remains clearly evident, the Chiba is built to purpose from the keel up; featuring numerous internal modifications and improvements including expanded fighter-handling facilities and dedicated launch tubes, the ship has greatly improved performance in the light carrier role. 

Identical in function to the original, the Chiba s commonly seen patrolling Terran space, serving as a a base for local policing efforts or as small task force leaders.

With the reconnection of Althes and Megnir gates came the hope of rediscovering the route to Aldrin sector. In preparation for such an event Pioneer engineers were tasked with preparing a transport vessel capable of ferrying enormous amounts of supplies and humanitarian aid for their long-lost families as soon as opportunity presents itself. The dawn of Project Genesis only expedited the development, promising a steady demand for such large transports.

The new flagship rivals the sheer bulk and mass of Intervention's battleship, the Asgard - with majority of the space dedicated to storage.

\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Entissus & Rothank\033X\

Developed by the Segaris Pioneers as a next-generation replacement for the aging pre-Shutdown era Mobile Mining Base Ship (MMBS), the Saga-class Ming and Recovery Command Vessel (MRCV) represents a major leap in autonomous resource operations. No longer limited to mining alone, the Saga brings integrated salvaging capabilities to the field, allowing it to process both asteroid and gaseous material, as well as derelict wreckage with equal efficiency. Heavily outfitted for defense, its L-sized turret hardpoints can mount military-grade weaponry when not equipped with mining tools, and its numerous M turrets provide solid protection against smaller threats. A high number of dedicated launch tubes enables simultaneous deployment and retrieval of drones without clogging landing pads, which remain free for S and M class support craft, such as escorts or supporting bulk transports. As both a logistical hub and a secure operational anchor, the Saga MRCV is a cornerstone of large-scale Segaris resource expeditions.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank, using assets from vanilla Tokyo and dTaco's X3 ATF-USC Ship Pack\033X\

A new development and seldom seen outside of Split space, the Cheetah is a light carrier created by Strong Arms designers as a more specifically tailored version of the old Split Panther. However, observers have noted that the Cheetah's unique capabilities are oddly well-suited to the lightning-fast ambush raids carried out by Fallen Families raiders, and the ship is just as commonly seen wearing Fallen Families colors as it is in Free Families livery, leading to a widely-accepted theory that the ship was in fact built to the specifications of an influential Fallen Families warband. 

Regardless of the truth of its origins, the Cheetah itself is an extremely capable raider - boasting an exceptionally high top speed along with an L-class turret hardpoint, a very large fighter capacity, and numerous launch tubes to rapidly surprise and overwhelm a target with fighters. However it is much less capable than its peers when it comes under direct threat, having poor shielding and only a small number of M-class defensive turrets. In addition, the Cheetah is fitted with relatively few landing pads, making it slow to recover its fighter complement. Alongside its limited capacity for self-defense against peer targets, this means that Cheetah captains must remain mindful of not only their attack vectors, but also be constantly planning an exit strategy should the tides of battle turn against them.

A cooperative effort between Boron and Argon engineers, the Marlin is a frigate built with lessons learned from encounters with Split and Xenon forces following the reconnection of Boron space to the wider Commonwealth. Having identified a need for anti-capital firepower Marlin is designed with a unique (among Boron vessels) primary weapon hardpoint capable of mounting large Commonwealth weaponry. Coupled with its small size and reduced price compared to a full destroyer, a squadron of Marlins can match the firepower of much larger vessels and overwhelm otherwise superior foes while maintaining cost parity.

Based on a heavily redesigned version of their previous Sturgeon hull, the Marlin represents a surprising breakthrough success for the returning Atraus Shipbuilding Currents corporation, providing their first foothold in the highly competitive military procurement market and placing them solidly in line with their older, more established corporate peers.

The Hammerhead - class Battleship, designed and constructed by the Atreus Shipbuilding Currents Corporation at the renowned Queen's Harbour shipyards, is a testament to Boron engineering focused on endurance and strategic dominance. Built to counteract the aggressive expansions of Strong Arms, this massive vessel serves as a resilient fleet anchor, embodying the Boron philosophy of survival and adaptability in warfare.

As the most heavily shielded warship in known space, the Hammerhead boasts unparalleled defensive capabilities, able to withstand relentless barrages that would cripple other battleships. Its extensive shield arrays and redundant energy systems ensure sustained performance under fire, making it a stalwart bastion in any conflict. However, this comes at the cost of firepower—its weapon systems are lackluster compared to the battleships of other factions, favoring energy - efficient and non-lethal solutions typical of Boron design.

With its ponderous speed and defensive orientation, the Hammerhead is less a blunt instrument of war and more a strategic keystone, designed to anchor fleet operations, soak up enemy fire, and support its allies with its enduring presence on the battlefield. This behemoth exemplifies the Boron's commitment to resilience, ensuring their fleets can outlast and outmaneuver more aggressive opponents.

The modern Solano is a highly advanced scout/interceptor hybrid. The standard fighter type deployed by OTAS, the Eurus is a well-rounded and capable combatant with respectable firepower and excellent high-speed manueverability. While it has few truly stand-out features aside from the high top speed, the ship enjoys a general advantage over its Commonwealth peers thanks to the advanced nature of OTAS technologies. The Eurus is a common sight in any location with an OTAS presence, serving on the offensive frontline and enforcing police presence in secured sectors.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Notus bomber was developed by OTAS during the isolation of the Great Dark. Initially just an exploratory testbed attempting to emulate the success of the M7M missile frigate- one of the many OTAS innovations of the pre-shutdown Commonwealth- the Notus performed well in simulations and exercises, promising to provide an immense amount of striking power with the ability to carry and deploy a wide variety of heavy ordnance in its modular side pods. When the gates abruptly reopened and OTAS resumed open hostilities against the Argon Federation, the Notus soon proved its worth and became notorious for savage lightning strikes capable of swiftly crippling Argon capital ships. 

Seeing an opportunity in their shared enemy, the Zyarth Patriarchy were quick to make diplomatic overtures towards OTAS, with the aim of procuring the Notus' technology for their own use. This effort culminated in the Split Wolf bomber and numerous improvements to the Notus, as well as new weapons that could take full advantage of the Notus-type ordnance hardpoint. The technology rapidly proliferated through the rest of the gate network, with the other Commonwealth powers and even the Terrans soon fielding their own bomber models- developed through espionage, battlefield salvage, or their own engineering efforts.

The modern Astraeus is a capable and versatile escort frigate: fast and fitting array of offensive and defensive turrets, and even possessing limited launch facilities for a handful of escort fighters. 

Though it lacks any forward-firing main armament, the unconventional shape of the hull and ample turret hardpoints allows the Astraeus to maintain surperb fields of fire all around itself, and it is often seen operating ahead or within formations of larger capital ships on anti-fighter picket duty.

Rumors abound that the ship makes use of highly illegal and dangerous AGI technology, though this has never been firmly proven despite intense scrutiny from both Commonwealth rivals and the Terran Protectorate.

Developed as an upgrade to the underperforming early Behemoth variants, the Erebus prioritizes survivability above all else, featuring unmatched defenses with four large shield generators - the most of any destroyer-type ship.

Its design philosophy revolves around redundancy and endurance, allowing it to withstand sustained assaults where others would falter. Armed exclusively with turret-based weaponry, the Erebus foregoes fixed mounts to focus on all-around coverage, making it a fortress in the depths of space. While it lacks the raw firepower of its peers, the Erebus excels in holding vital and hazardous positions, ensuring prolonged sector defense with unshakable reliability.

The Ingrid is a mysterious and advanced fighter developed in secret by Tidebreak engineers, believed to be the final project of the famed Sihi Do - the same mind behind the Erlking battleship. Like its capital-sized sibling, the Ingrid can withstand all kinds of region damage, such as Avarice's tide - a unique and rare trait. Though externally it appears similar to Windfall’s fighters like the Kyd or Lux, the Ingrid is vastly superior in engineering, performance, and construction quality.

Despite its small size, the Ingrid is built with cutting-edge materials and equipped with a weapon system larger and far more advanced than what is typically found in the Syndicate’s mass-produced fleets or even other Commonwealth faction rosters. The ship's internal systems are intricate and maintenance-heavy, making it a poor choice for mass deployment but an ideal platform for elite pilots, clandestine missions, and high-risk escort operations. Its unmatched resilience and agility caught the attention of the Terran Secret Service, who reportedly launched an investigation into its origins, naming it "Khopesh". Additionally, the OTAS Corporation’s Eurus fighter bears striking similarities to the Ingrid, fueling speculation of corporate espionage or black market blueprint trading, though no conclusive evidence has surfaced.

Production of the Ingrid was never formalized - its complexity and cost proving too great for the fragmented industrial base of the Riptide Rakers. Some say one or two prototypes were completed and hidden away; others claim the ship was handed off to trusted, but anonymous, allies in Windfall or even Terran hands. Whatever the truth, the Ingrid represents a glimpse into what the Rakers might have become had their technological ambitions not been drowned by isolation, scarcity, and political strife - a ghost of potential, wrapped in myth.

Developed and employed by the Riptide Rakers as a stopgap measure to assist large ships which were crippled by the Tide but could be saved, the Douala is a small and simple utility vessel suitable for use the confined space around Tidebreak station. A minimalist design intended to only be deployed over short distances in the hectic periods between Tides, the Douala is sluggish, lightly shielded, and completely unarmed save for a single repair beam. The ship's primary defining feature is a set of bulky storage units capable of housing a small handful of repair drones for transfer to a larger ship, as the Douala lacks the size or facilities to deploy them itself.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

The Fireship is a crude combat drone fielded by the Vigor Syndicate, assembled from salvaged wreckage and spare parts with little regard for longevity. Unshielded and barely held together, it carries a brutal complement of dumbfire missiles capable of crippling larger vessels. Once its munitions are expended, the drone becomes a harmless distraction for enemy turrets, lacking any capacity for reloading in the field. Designed as a one-way weapon, the Fireship boasts exceptional firepower for its size but is rarely expected - or intended - to survive its assault.\n\n\033#95e03b29#Ship model by: Rothank\033X\

Fitted with multiple turrets, the Vulture Raider boasts significantly improved defensive firepower compared to its civilian counterpart. However, like most Raider-class vessels, it is a patchwork of modifications, often poorly maintained and riddled with jury-rigged systems. Its cramped and barely livable interior reflects its purpose - mixing relatively high cargo space with extreme defensive capabilities while minimizing anything unrelated to profit or survival.

A far cry from even the poorly-kept Vulture freighters of legitimate merchants, the Vulture Raider is typically riddled with external damage, missing panels, and exposed wiring. Its extremely low resale value makes it a ship that few would willingly purchase - except for those desperate or reckless enough to take advantage of its firepower and hauling capacity, regardless of the risks.

Designed to support a large crew for extended raids, the interior is a cramped and barely livable mess, with hastily retrofitted bunks and repurposed cargo holds serving as crew quarters. Like most Raider-class ships, it is poorly maintained, often battle-scarred, and held together by desperation and necessity. With a reputation of a deathtrap, the Osprey Raider is a ship that only the most daring - or reckless - pirates would dare call home.

To compensate for its added weight, two additional engines have been haphazardly grafted onto the hull, giving the Osprey Raider a surprising turn of speed, unsurprisingly - at the cost of reliability. The original landing pad has been completely stripped out, replaced with an oversized torpedo storage bay and launch tubes, allowing it to unleash devastating barrages far beyond what a typical corvette could manage.

Another revived design borne of the increasing cooperation within the Scale Plate Pact, the Blastclaw bomber is a remarkably capable ship and is a common sight in among larger pirate flotillas, both escorting larger vessels and operating as an independent strike wing. 

Though rather slow, the ship is well-shielded and features a heavily reinforced hull. However, the true strength of the bomber lies in the Incendiary Bomb Mortar mounted under the cockpit, capable of rapidly blasting away exposed surface elements and weakening shielded hulls. Even a single Blastclaw poses a deadly threat to poorly defended freighters, while a sufficient number of them can even challenge and disarm a destroyer, leaving it disabled and vulnerable to boarding actions undertaken by larger ships.

Another of the Scale Plate Pact's homegrown designs, the Marauder corvette was first created in an act of desperation by a mechanically inclined Pact captain whose Minotaur Raider had been crippled in a raid gone awry. Though he managed to limp back to a hidden freeport, survival was only the first of his problems. Financially destitute, with a shattered ship and a crew on the verge of desertion, the captain - one Iljorgawas Minanoros Ioannis XII - noticed that although the central section of his Minotaur was little more than twisted scrap, the critical forward control and the aft machinery sections were still mostly intact. Struck by a flash of inspiration, he managed to cajole a little more faith from his crew and spent the next several days cutting out the damaged central section of his ship and reconnecting the two remaining portions. A few modifications later, he and his crew once again headed out in what would become the template design for the Marauder. 

As the smallest medium-class ship currently found in the Gate Network, the Marauder specializes in attacking smaller foes while running from larger ones with its good agility and comparatively high speed. A varied collection of armaments - a pair of M-class fixed mounts, a single M-class turret, and four S-class fixed mounts thrown in for good measure - gives the ship good striking power against small transporters or enemy fighters, while the surprisingly capacious cargo storage for its size allows SCA freebooters to haul home their spoils. In exchange, the poor shielding, somewhat questionable hull strength, and anemic armament for its weight class leaves the ship with unfavorable odds when facing other corvettes or even a particularly ornery heavy fighter pilot. Nonetheless, its low operating costs and cheap construction price(often made cheaper through the use of written-off Minotaurs, like the original) ensure its place as a mainstay among the Scale Plate Pact pirates.

One of the larger threats in regular use by the Scale Plate Pact, the Brigantine is a heavily armed capital ship that can pose a significant threat even to military forces. Found almost anywhere that Scale Plate pirates operate and fulfilling any role demanded of it from solo raider to warband leader, the ship's pervasive presence in pirate fleets is owed primarily to its relative ease of acquisition. As many observers have concluded from it's appearance, the Brigantine is cobbled together by pirate shipwrights using the hull sections of Teladi auxiliary ships and carriers- scavenged from battlefield wrecks, decommissioned hulks and even the occasional captured prize. As with the Galleon, rumors abound of the Scale Plate Pact employing less overt means of acquiring these hulls through independent purchasers or unscrupulous Teladi officials, though the Teladi Company vehemently denies the rumors as slander and the Pact remains characteristically cagey with its secrets. 

In the battlespace, the Brigantine employs a typically mismatched grab bag of weaponry and shielding, with the pirates making up what they lack in sophistication and planning with enthusiasm and sheer volume of fire. A handful of docking pads and launch tubes- remnants of the original ships that make up the hull- allows the Brigantine to deploy and support a small wing of fighters or drones to bolster its already-formidable firepower, while cavernous cargo capacity alleviates any need to be picky with plundered loot. Even the sheer imposing size of the vessel offers another weapon in the form of a menacing intimidation factor against civilian freighters. However, the design has numerous flaws as well- the nature of the Brigantine's construction leaves it with a weak hull structure for a ship of its size, a problem made worse by the relatively limited shielding and subpar speed. The substantial armament is also widely distributed across the hull, leaving few blind spots but in turn greatly degrading the ship's ability to concentrate fire on a target.
